steps.observation: You have 300 seconds. Name three causes of World War I.

steps.action:
Here are three major long-term causes of World War I:

1. Militarism  
   European powers engaged in an unprecedented arms race, building huge armies and navies. This glorification of military strength made diplomatic solutions harder and raised the chance that any crisis would be met with force.

2. Alliance System  
   By 1914 Europe was divided into two rival blocs—the Triple Entente (Britain, France, Russia) and the Triple Alliance (Germany, Austria-Hungary, Italy). These binding commitments turned what might have been a localized conflict into a general war.

3. Nationalism  
   Intense national pride and aspirations (e.g. Slavic independence movements in the Balkans, French revanchism against Germany) fueled mutual distrust and made compromise more difficult.
